headline.purpose: Page-level headings and prominent dashboard summaries.

components.name: Primary Button
components.css: .ds-button-primary { background: #0D9488; color: #FFFFFF; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 24px; font: 600 14px/1.25 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms ease; } .ds-button-primary:hover { background: #0F766E; } .ds-button-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0D9488; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-button-primary:active { background: #0F766E; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Lower-priority action with a quiet border.
components.css: .ds-button-secondary { background: #FFFFFF; color: #475569; border: 1px solid #E2E8F0; border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 16px; font: 400 14px/1.5 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms ease; } .ds-button-secondary:hover { background: #F8FAFC; } .ds-button-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0D9488; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Input
components.description: Labeled field with a visible teal focus state.
components.css: .ds-field { display: grid; gap: 4px; color: #334155; font: 600 12px/1.5 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-input { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; background: #FFFFFF; color: #334155; border: 1px solid #E2E8F0; border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 12px; font: 400 14px/1.5 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: #0D9488; outline: 2px solid #CCFBF1; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Card
components.description: White content surface on the cool canvas.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #FFFFFF; color: #334155; border: 1px solid #E2E8F0; border-radius: 16px; padding: 24px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); font: 400 14px/1.5 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-card h2 { margin: 0 0 8px; color: #12304A; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; } .ds-card p { margin: 0; }

components.name: Active Navigation Item
components.description: Selected destination with a quiet teal state.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; background: #CCFBF1; color: #0F766E; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 12px; font: 500 14px/1.5 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 150ms ease; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: #B5F5EA; } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0D9488; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
ToothCare Hub should feel like a capable clinic team: calm, clear, and dependable. Its existing deep-navy structure, restrained teal actions, cool light canvas, and Inter typography already establish a coherent healthcare identity. Preserve and formalize that visual language rather than replacing it with a new brand.

The interface is an operational tool, not a medical-marketing campaign. Make the next action and the appointment facts easy to find. Patient booking should communicate progress and selection clearly; admin and dentist views should prioritize the work each role needs to scan. Reuse shared patterns without flattening those different priorities.

This design record describes the existing React/Vite/Tailwind JSX prototype and the approved direction for future frontend work. TypeScript and shadcn/ui are goals in the project brief, not libraries currently evidenced in the frontend package or source.
keyCharacteristics: Deep navy provides stable structure; teal marks action and selection.
Cool, light surfaces keep forms and schedules legible.
Inter and compact, consistent type hierarchy support frequent scanning.
Shared patterns adapt to patient, admin, and dentist tasks.
Accessibility and responsive behavior are design requirements, not a claim of conformance.

rules.name: The Navy-for-Structure Rule
rules.body: Keep navy on navigation, headers, and high-priority headings; do not make every card or action a navy block.

rules.name: The Teal-for-Action Rule
rules.body: Reserve the strongest teal treatment for primary actions, progress, and selected states. Do not use the action color as a substitute for status meaning.

dos: Do use the existing navy, teal, cool-canvas, and Inter identity as the baseline for new frontend screens.
Do reserve teal for primary actions, progress, and selected states.
Do give each role's dashboard a task-specific information hierarchy while sharing component behavior.
Do use semantic HTML, labels, keyboard access, visible focus, readable contrast, and responsive layouts.
Do pair status color with text and keep sensitive health details out of decorative or unnecessary UI surfaces.
donts: Don't replace the established palette or typography without an explicit redesign decision.
Don't imply WCAG conformance until the rendered interface has been tested.
Don't present TypeScript or shadcn/ui as already installed or implemented.
Don't use color alone for appointment status or form errors.
Don't change backend behavior, database structure, API contracts, or appointment workflows as part of a visual-system task.
